title: Alert annotator and commit-scan playbook
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, repeatable workflow for the first 60–90 minutes after a production perf alert fires. It focuses on quick signal enrichment ("annotator" step), a lightweight commit-scan (fast bisection-ish approach), and a deterministic canary vs baseline comparison method we can run without heavy manual sorting.

Why this is different:
- Intentionally lightweight so on-call can close the loop quickly or handoff with a high-signal hypothesis.
- Emphasizes annotation (why did alert fire, customer-visible impact, likely severity) so downstream owners can prioritize.
- Uses a deterministic harness (shadow-run and synthetic traces) to reduce flakiness in comparisons.

Quick triage checklist (first 15 min):
1) Annotate the alert in PagerDuty/Alert manager: brief sentence with observed metric, region, and sample request id (if present).
   - Example: "p95 latency spike in us-west-2, model=redwood-7b, sample_trace=trace-9a4f"
2) Snapshot the fast metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, errors/s, inflight_requests, batch_size_distribution, kvcache_evictions_total, cpu_utilization, gpu_utilization.
   - Grafana panels: latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, latency_p99_ms, request_error_rate, batch_size_histogram, kvcache_eviction_rate
3) Check recent deploys and autoscaler activity for the region + model (last 2 hours). Look for new images, infra churn, or sudden scale-down/up events.

Signal enrichment (annotator) — add context to the alert:
- Affected model(s) and pinned version(s).
- Ingress pattern: short-requests vs long generation; sample prompt length distribution.
- Canary tags: was there a canary deployment active? If so, list canary id and routes.
- Customer impact: is any customer reporting errors or increased latency? Add links to customer threads.
- Attach 2–3 representative trace IDs (from distributed tracing) and 1 synthetic request that reproduces the increased latency.

Sampling strategy to reduce noise:
- Pull 200 requests around the spike window (+/- 5m) and cluster by prompt length and batch size.
- Prefer synthetic runs for deterministic comparisons (see harness below).
- When using live traces, group by root cause tags: kvcache_hit=false, backend_retries>0, gpu_queue_delay>50ms.

Deterministic canary vs baseline comparison (20–40 min):
Objective: decide if the behavior is reproducible and whether it maps to code/infra changes.
Steps:
1) Identify baseline commit: last known-good deployment tag (e.g., release/2025-01-21).
2) Identify suspect commit range: all deploys in last 48h that touch serving runtime, kernel selection, batching controller, or cache code.
3) Run shadow-synthetic test harness across both commits (baseline + suspect):
   - Use same input corpus (200 prompts sampled from production window) and fixed RNG seed.
   - Run at target concurrency equal to the observed peak inflight requests.
   - Capture latency percentiles, batch-size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, and GPU queue time.

Example harness invocation (internal tool names are illustrative):
- python tools/perf_shadow/runner.py --model redwood-7b --commit release/2025-01-21 --input sample-200.json --concurrency 48 --out /tmp/baseline.json
- python tools/perf_shadow/runner.py --model redwood-7b --commit HEAD~3 --input sample-200.json --concurrency 48 --out /tmp/suspect.json
- python tools/perf_shadow/compare.py --left /tmp/baseline.json --right /tmp/suspect.json --metrics latency_p50,latency_p95,kvcache_hit_rate,batch_size_mean

Fast commit-scan (a pragmatic alternative to full git-bisect):
- If suspect range > 6 commits, do exponential scan: test HEAD, HEAD~4, HEAD~8, HEAD~16 until you cross the boundary where the regression appears (binary-ish but fewer runs).
- Narrow to a 3–5 commit window, then test each commit sequentially with the harness.
- Record the first commit that shows the delta consistently across 3 runs.

What to capture in the hypothesis log (quick):
- hypothesis_id: HYP-20250301-01
- root signal: p95 latency + kvcache_evictions_up
- suspected cause: batching controller change in PR #1729 or kernel fallback for attention in cuda-12.2
- reproducibility: yes/no (attach harness results)
- next action: revert candidate / throttle canary / escalate to infra

Common signal fingerprints and quick checks:
- GPU queue tail latencies + growth in batch_size variance => scheduling or kernel fallback issue.
- Sudden increase in kvcache evictions_total => cache eviction regression or increased memory pressure.
- Elevated cpu_utilization but low gpu_utilization => CPU-side serialization, e.g., tokenization, batching controller.
- Spiky autoshutdowns or pod restarts => infra/oomkilling or container image problems.

When to escalate immediately:
- Errors > 1% of requests for high-priority customers or safety-related endpoints.
- Latency increase that causes timeouts downstream (observed 5xx from gateway).
- Failed canary rollout with >2% deviation in p95 across two consecutive checks.

Communication templates (copy/paste) — initial alert annotation:
- Subject: [ANN] perf spike us-west-2 — redwood-7b — p95 x2
- Body: "Observed p95 latency increase (1200ms -> 2800ms) in us-west-2 for redwood-7b. Sample trace ids: trace-9a4f, trace-9ab1. Snapshot attached: baseline vs suspect harness outputs. Preliminary hypothesis: batching controller change (PR#1729) increased batch-size variance leading to GPU queue spikes. Running commit-scan now."

Post-handoff checklist:
- Attach harness outputs and comparison CSV to the incident ticket.
- Create a short playbook item for the owner: reproduce, fix, canary-verify, cut a rollback candidate.
- If revert is required, prefer emergency-rollback procedure with canary throttling rather than full global rollback where possible.
- Schedule a 1-hour follow-up meeting within 24h to finalize RCA and next steps.

Persistent tooling ideas (follow-ups / backlog):
- Small UI to run the exponential commit-scan from the incident UI and auto-attach outputs.
- A lightweight annotator Slack slash command to create the initial hypothesis entry and ping the on-call owner.
- Synthetic corpus manager: keep curated prompt sets per model and per workload (short, medium, long) for deterministic comparisons.

Appendix — quick queries and panel recipes:
- Grafana: query for p95 latency by model and region: sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{le="0.95"}[5m])) by (model, region) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (model, region)
- KV cache eviction rate: increase(kvcache_evictions_total[10m]) by (shard, model)
- GPU queue time (custom histogram metric): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_queue_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance))

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need a small experiment to validate that synthetic shadow-runs reproduce production kvcache eviction patterns.
- Decide SLO for canary deviation thresholds that should auto-pause a rollout (proposal: p95 deviation > 30% for 5m).

If you end up owning the follow-up, ping me (Priya) and I’ll hand over the harness script and the sample corpora.

-- end of playbook --
